arxiv-2011-13264.title: Gödel and Gödel-type solutions in the Palatini f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity theory
arxiv-2011-13264.creator: J. S. Gonçalves, A. F. Santos
arxiv-2011-13264.description: Abstract The Palatini f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity theory is considered. The standard Einstein-Hilbert action is replaced by an arbitrary function of the Ricci scalar R R and of the trace T T of the energy-momentum tensor. In the Palatini approach, the Ricci scalar is a function of the metric and the connection.

arxiv-2103-04628.title: Personalized Federated Learning using Hypernetworks
arxiv-2103-04628.creator: Aviv Shamsian ∗, Aviv Navon ∗, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik, Aviv Shamsian ∗, Aviv Navon ∗, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik
arxiv-2103-04628.description: Abstract Personalized federated learning is tasked with training machine learning models for multiple clients, each with its own data distribution. The goal is to train personalized models in a collaborative way while accounting for data disparities across clients and reducing communication costs. We propose a novel approach to this problem using hypernetworks, termed pFedHN for personalized Federated HyperNetworks .

arxiv-2111-11858.title: Asteroid Flyby Cycler Trajectory Design Using Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2111-11858.creator: Naoya Ozaki, Kanta Yanagida, Takuya Chikazawa, Nishanth Pushparaj, Naoya Takeishi, Ryuki Hyodo
arxiv-2111-11858.description: Abstract Asteroid exploration has been attracting more attention in recent years. Nevertheless, we have just visited tens of asteroids while we have discovered more than one million bodies. As our current observation and knowledge should be biased, it is essential to explore multiple asteroids directly to better understand the remains of planetary building materials.

arxiv-2303-16287.title: Lower Bounds for Pseudo-Deterministic Counting in a Stream
arxiv-2303-16287.creator: Vladimir Braverman, Robert Krauthgamer, Aditya Krishnan, Shay Sapir
arxiv-2303-16287.description: Abstract Many streaming algorithms provide only a high-probability relative approximation. These two relaxations, of allowing approximation and randomization, seem necessary – for many streaming problems, both relaxations must be employed simultaneously, to avoid an exponentially larger (and often trivial) space complexity.

arxiv-2407-10112.title: Warming Up Cold-Start CTR Prediction by Learning Item-Specific Feature Interactions
arxiv-2407-10112.creator: Yaqing Wang, Hongming Piao, Daxiang Dong, Quanming Yao, Jingbo Zhou
arxiv-2407-10112.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yaqing Wang, Hongming Piao, Daxiang Dong, Quanming Yao, Jingbo Zhou. In recommendation systems, new items are continuously introduced, initially lacking interaction records but gradually accumulating them over time. Accurately predicting the click-through rate (CTR) for these items is crucial for enhancing both revenue and user experience. While existing methods focus on enhancing item ID embeddings for new items within general CTR models, they tend to adopt a global feature interaction approach, often overshadowing new items with sparse data by those with abundant interactions.

arxiv-2502-01068.title: FastKV: Decoupling of Context Reduction and KV Cache Compression for Prefill-Decoding Acceleration
arxiv-2502-01068.creator: Dongwon Jo, Jiwon Song, Yulhwa Kim, Jae-Joon Kim
arxiv-2502-01068.description: Abstract While large language models (LLMs) excel at handling long-context sequences, they require substantial prefill computation and key-value (KV) cache, which can heavily burden computational efficiency and memory usage in both prefill and decoding stages. Recent works that compress KV caches with prefill acceleration reduce this cost but inadvertently tie the prefill compute reduction to the decoding KV budget.

arxiv-2509-17428.title: QWHA: Quantization-Aware Walsh-Hadamard Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-17428.creator: Hyesung Jeon, Seojune Lee, Beomseok Kang, Yulhwa Kim, Jae-Joon Kim
arxiv-2509-17428.description: Abstract The demand for efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) has driven interest in quantization, which reduces inference cost, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), which lowers training overhead. This motivated the development of quantization-aware PEFT to produce accurate yet efficient quantized models. In this setting, reducing quantization error prior to fine-tuning is crucial for achieving high model accuracy.

arxiv-2510-23609.title: A short survey on almost orthogonal vectors in a few specific large dimensions
arxiv-2510-23609.creator: ℝ \mathbb{R} ami Luisto
arxiv-2510-23609.description: Abstract . The concept of almost orthogonal vectors , i.e. vectors whose cosine similarity is close to 0 0 , relates to topics both in pure mathematics and in coding theory under the guises of spherical packing and spherical codes.

arxiv-2512-17253.title: Mitty: Diffusion-based Human-to-Robot Video Generation
arxiv-2512-17253.creator: Yiren SongCheng LiuWeijia Mao, Mike Zheng Shou
arxiv-2512-17253.description: Abstract Learning directly from human demonstration videos is a key milestone toward scalable and generalizable robot learning. Yet existing methods rely on intermediate representations such as keypoints or trajectories, introducing information loss and cumulative errors that harm temporal and visual consistency. We present Mitty, a Diffusion Transformer that enables video In-Context Learning for end-to-end Human2Robot video generation.

plos-pone-0004529.creator: Florian Hartmut Seeger, Linping Chen, Ioakim Spyridopoulos et al.
plos-pone-0004529.description: PLOS ONE research article. Transplantation of vasculogenic progenitor cells (VPC) improves neovascularization after ischemia. However, patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus show a reduced VPC number and impaired functional activity. Previously, we demonstrated that p38 kinase inhibition prevents the negat

pmc-10660828.title: Global Health Mentorship: Challenges and Opportunities for Equitable Partnership
pmc-10660828.creator: Luchuo Engelbert Bain, Brenda Mbouamba Yankam, Jude Dzevela Kong, Ngwayu Claude Nkfusai, Oluwaseun Abdulganiyu Badru, Ikenna Desmond Ebuenyi, Azeez Butali, Nicholas Kofi Adjei, Oluwafemi Adeagbo
pmc-10660828.description: inant of equitable, sustainable and inclusive improvements in health outcomes globally. Researchers from the Global South face unique global health mentorship challenges. Some of these challenges include: limited opportunities, access to mentorship opportunities, lack of a healthy mentorship culture, weak and insufficient institutional support, language barriers (non-English speakers) and colonial mentorship mindset.

pmc-11385719.title: Genome sequences of 36 Streptococcus pneumoniae strains optimized for the multiplexed opsonophagocytosis killing assay
pmc-11385719.creator: Emma Graffice, Chloe Meewes, Feroze A. Ganaie, Moon H. Nahm, Juan J. Calix
pmc-11385719.description: A multiplexed opsonophagocytosis assay (MOPA) was developed as a cost-effective, high-throughput biological assay to evaluate the efficacy of pneumococcal vaccines by in vitro measurement of opsonophagocytic activity of anti-capsular antibodies. Here, we report draft genomes of the 36 strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae developed for use in the reference pneumococcal MOPA.

pmc-11456242.title: 25-hydroxycholesterol promotes brain cytokine production and leukocyte infiltration in a mouse model of lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation
pmc-11456242.creator: Johnathan Romero, Danira Toral-Rios, Jinsheng Yu, Steven M Paul, Anil G Cashikar
pmc-11456242.description: Neuroinflammation has been implicated in the pathogenesis of several neurologic and psychiatric disorders. Microglia are key drivers of neuroinflammation and, in response to different inflammatory stimuli, overexpress a proinflammatory signature of genes. Among these, Ch25h is a gene overexpressed in brain tissue from Alzheimer’s disease as well as various mouse models of neuroinflammation.

pmc-11466797.title: Unveiling the imprinted dance: how parental genomes orchestrate seed development and hybrid success
pmc-11466797.creator: Muthusamy Muthusamy, Subramani Pandian, Eun-Kyuong Shin, Ho-Keun An, Soo-In Sohn
pmc-11466797.description: Parental epigenetic asymmetries, which contribute to the monoallelic expression of genes known as imprints, play a critical role in seed development in flowering plants. Primarily, differential DNA methylation patterns and histone modifications on parental alleles form the molecular basis of gene imprinting. Plants predominantly exhibit this non-Mendelian inheritance phenomenon in the endosperm and the early embryo of developing seeds.

pmc-11527322.title: HTL/KAI2 signaling substitutes for light to control plant germination
pmc-11527322.creator: Jenna E. Hountalas, Michael Bunsick, Zhenhua Xu, Andrea A. Taylor, Gianni Pescetto, George Ly, François-Didier Boyer, Christopher S. P. McErlean, Shelley Lumba, Claudia Köhler, Caroline Gutjahr, Claudia Köhler, Caroline Gutjahr, Claudia Köhler, Caroline Gutjahr, Claudia Köhler, Caroline Gutjahr
pmc-11527322.description: Plants monitor multiple environmental cues, such as light and temperature, to ensure they germinate at the right time and place. Some specialist plants, like ephemeral fire-following weeds and root parasitic plants, germinate primarily in response to small molecules found in specific environments.

pmc-11721858.title: Approaches to a crisis in early pregnancy: an explorative qualitative study of medical students and doctors in training in Ireland, using a story completion model
pmc-11721858.creator: Mary Higgins, Sharon Cooley, Deirdre Hayes-Ryan, Brendan Dempsey
pmc-11721858.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A crisis in early pregnancy can be due to an unplanned pregnancy or a suspected abnormality. Pregnant people have the right to unbiased and comprehensive advice of all options from healthcare providers. Using story completion models (SCM), the aim of this qualitative study was to explore the attitudes of medical students and doctors in training towards crisis pregnancy, specifically two scenarios: early unplanned pregnancy and fatal fetal abnormality (anencephaly).

pmc-12421768.title: Caffeine mitigates ROS accumulation and attenuates motor neuron degeneration in the wobbler mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
pmc-12421768.creator: Aimo Samuel Christian Epplen, Maximilian Rothöft, Sarah Stahlke, Carsten Theiss, Veronika Matschke
pmc-12421768.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAmyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a devastating neurodegenerative disease characterized by oxidative stress and progressive motor neuron degeneration. This study evaluates the potential neuroprotective effects of caffeine in the Wobbler mouse, an established model of ALS.MethodsWobbler mice received caffeine supplementation (60 mg/kg/day) via drinking water, and key parameters, including muscle strength, NAD metabolism, oxidative stress, and motor neuron morphology, were assessed at critical disease stages.ResultsCaffeine delayed motor performance decline, as observed in grip strength tests during the early symptomatic phase.

pmc-12552567.title: Mitochondria-enriched nanovesicles: A novel approach for treating radiation-induced skin injury
pmc-12552567.creator: Mengru Zhu, Junhao Xia, Jia Liu, Wei Zou, Xin Guan, Lizhi Wang, Yichen Wang, Bing Wang, Fengya Wang, Qingwen Zhang, Keman He, Lukuan Liu, Jing Liu
pmc-12552567.description: Radiation-induced skin injury (RSI) is characterized by persistent mitochondrial dysfunction and compromised DNA repair mechanisms, posing significant challenges for clinical management. To address this, we engineered mitochondria-enriched nanovesicles (NVs) derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUMSCs), designed to deliver bioactive mitochondrial components to irradiated skin tissues.

pmc-12753636.title: Characterisation of human in vitro tumour-associated macrophage models to define translational relevance
pmc-12753636.creator: Arthur Dyer, Rebecca Dudley, Shreya Ahuja, Clara Alsinet, Pawan Poudel, Georgina Bowyer, Kalvin Sahota, Saly Songvilay, Des C. Jones, Matthew Glover, Sonja Hess, Elina Timosenko, Simon J. Dovedi
pmc-12753636.description: Tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key components of the tumour microenvironment with a demonstrated ability to modulate anti-tumour T-cell responses and immunotherapy outcomes. With increasing realisation that the M1/M2 paradigm does not reflect the complexity of macrophage phenotypes in cancer patients, an urgent need has arisen to develop improved, translatable in vitro models for human TAMs.

pmc-12824158.title: Effect of temperature on the wetting performance of coal powder by different surfactant solutions: experimental and molecular dynamics simulation study
pmc-12824158.creator: Wei Fu, Jianhong Kang, Wenxu Liang, Pengjiang Deng
pmc-12824158.description: Current research on coal dust wettability primarily focuses on surfactant types, concentrations, and coal properties, while the role of temperature as a key parameter in practical applications has not been fully explored. This study combines experimental measurements and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to systematically investigate the influence of temperature (291.15–308.

pmc-13041110.title: Psychological and behavioral mechanisms that drive medical staff’s engagement in kidney palliative care—an empirical analysis from medical staff in mainland China
pmc-13041110.creator: Wenbo Zhu, Meijie Wu, Shuo Zhang, Ru Li, Tiejun Liu, Yue Zhou, Yuxia Guan, Jinghua Xia
pmc-13041110.description: BackgroundThe high medical costs of continuous treatment for end-stage renal disease impose significant financial strain on patients and their families, highlighting the need for palliative care. However, the development of renal PC in mainland China remains hindered by substantial challenges.

pmc-13090008.title: Film, function, flexibility: label-free nanobody sensors via electropolymerized nanointerfaces
pmc-13090008.creator: Daniel P. Carroll, Imen Boumar, Anna M. Kotowska, David J. Scurr, Paula M. Mendes
pmc-13090008.description: Nanobody-based biosensors promise exceptional molecular recognition and robustness, but their implementation has been limited by unstable and non-scalable surface chemistries. Here we introduce a materials platform that integrates stable electropolymerized tyramine nanofilms with label-free, non-faradaic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for direct molecular detection.

pmc-13233687.title: Atypical X-linked agammaglobulinemia diagnosed in adulthood with arthritis caused by a hypomorphic BTK splice-site variant: a case report and literature review
pmc-13233687.creator: Asuka Takayama, Kazuyuki Meguro, Masaya Yokota, Takahiro Sugiyama, Shunjiro Kurihara, Masaki Hiraguri, Hirokazu Kanegane, Hiroshi Nakajima
pmc-13233687.description: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA) is an inborn error of immunity (IEI) caused by loss-of-function variants in the Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) gene, classically presenting in early childhood with recurrent bacterial infections. Here, we report an atypical case of XLA diagnosed in adulthood during evaluation of inflammatory arthritis.

pmc-13276275.title: Long‐term trends in metabolic profiles across Chinese birth cohorts: A real‐world big data analysis
pmc-13276275.creator: Ying Xiong, Xincen Duan, Jing Zhu, Jiayi Huang, Baishen Pan, Wenqi Shao, Beili Wang, Wei Guo
pmc-13276275.description: BackgroundThe global burden of metabolic diseases is increasingly severe, with a continuous rise in prevalence among younger populations. There is an urgent need to explore the long‐term trends of metabolic risk factors across generations. This study aimed to investigate birth cohort effects on metabolic profiles among Chinese adults to provide a basis for precision prevention and control.

pmc-13295690.title: Biochemical, Immunohistochemical and Behavioral Effects of Spexin in a Methimazole-Induced Hypothyroidism Rat Model
pmc-13295690.creator: Seda Koçak, Gülhan Ünlü, Kübra Tuğçe Kalkan, Ferhat Pektaş, Ahmet Türk

pmc-13335325.title: An investigation of theoretical model of the relationship between discussion with families and the attitude toward organ donation in Iran: the mediating role of Spiritual Well-Being
pmc-13335325.creator: Hamid Sharif-Nia, Noushin Mousazadeh, Mahnaz Rakhshan, Roghye Nazari, Maryam Dehghani, Hamideh Hakimi, Setayeshi Jafari BenahKhalkhal
pmc-13335325.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThere is still a serious imbalance between the number of organ donors and the number of patients on the transplant list. It is therefore of great importance to assess and strengthen resources to improve people’s attitudes towards organ donation. This study examines the possible mediating role of Spiritual Well-Being (SWB) in relation to attitudes towards organ donation and family discussions in Iranian society.MethodsThis is a cross-sectional study conducted in Iran in 2022.

pmc-13359936.title: Load–velocity relationship during chain-based variable resistance in the smith machine back squat
pmc-13359936.creator: Zhuorong Huang, Jie Li, Zhaoqian Li, Xing Zhang, Ruizhi Liu, Zongwei Chen, Xiuli Zhang, Amador García-Ramos
pmc-13359936.description: BackgroundVelocity-based training (VBT) is well established for prescribing and monitoring intensity in traditional constant resistance training; however, its applicability to chain-based variable resistance training has not been examined. This study examined how different magnitudes of chain-based variable resistance influence commonly used VBT-derived metrics.MethodsThirty-four resistance-trained men (age: 20.50 ± 2.00 years, constant-load one-repetition maximum [1RM]: 1.85 ± 0.

pmc-13457881.title: Deep learning algorithm for automatic detection of acute ischemic stroke on noncontrast brain CT
pmc-13457881.creator: Tae Jin Yun, Jin Wook Choi, Hoon Na, Miran Han, Woo Sang Jung, Ji Ye Lee, Roh-Eul Yoo, In Pyeong Hwang, Seung Hong Choi
pmc-13457881.description: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a deep learning-based algorithm for detecting acute ischemic stroke (AIS), including small infarcts, on non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT). A retrospective, multi-reader, pivotal, crossover, randomized study involving 917 cases was conducted to validate the performance of an artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm.

pmc-13476123.title: Piezoelectric shaping of radical mastoid cavity and dissection of ossified cochlea prior to cochlear implantation
pmc-13476123.creator: Samiah S Al-Angari, Marc Bloching, Katharina Stölzel, Stefan Lyutenski
pmc-13476123.description: Cochlear implantation (CI) in radical cavities remains challenging due to the risk of postoperative electrode extrusion. We report a single-stage approach employing piezoelectric instrument (PEI) to optimize cavity osteoplasty, atraumatic cochlear access, and electrode stabilization in the setting of partial scala tympani ossification.

pmc-13501294.title: Relation extraction for diet, non-communicable disease and biomarker associations (RECoDe): a CoDiet study
pmc-13501294.creator: Donghee Choi, Yajie Gu, Kai Qi Zong, Antoine D Lain, Dimitrios Zaikis, Thomas Rowlands, Marek Rei, The CoDiet Consortium, Tim Beck, Joram M Posma

pmc-13682702.title: The Neuroendocrine-Cardiovascular Axis in Chronic Kidney Disease: The Role of Prolactin and Gonadal Dysfunction
pmc-13682702.creator: Vincenzo Barbera, Luca Di Lullo, Antonio Bellasi, Lorenzo D’Elia, Annalisa Villani, Paola Peverini, Aldo Franculli
pmc-13682702.description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) is accompanied by endocrine disturbances, including elevated prolactin and disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Their reproductive consequences are well recognized, whereas their cardiovascular relevance remains uncertain.SummaryReduced renal metabolism, altered dopaminergic regulation, the uremic milieu, inflammation, and comorbidity may increase prolactin and suppress gonadal function. In men, testosterone deficiency becomes more common as kidney function declines.
